note: Conservative, machine-oriented bridge-lemma templates suggested by the 3 SF1 Multiset RC1 failures. These are NOT claimed novel; most are 'probably_existing' in Mathlib (e.g. Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_nsmul, Finset.disjoint_left, Finset.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem). The dominant signal is that the *bridge lemmas already exist* but RC1's Multiset induction oracle does not deploy them — the real gap is an ext+membership-simp tactic family, not a new lemma. Templates are recorded so SF3 can test utility either way.

candidates.informal_description: Membership in a multiset's toFinset coincides with membership in the multiset.
candidates.lean_statement_sketch: theorem mem_toFinset {s : Multiset α} {a : α} : a ∈ s.toFinset ↔ a ∈ s
candidates.proof_family_hint: simp/decide on Multiset.toFinset definition; this is the universal simp bridge for all three failures

candidates.informal_description: Two multisets' toFinsets are Finset-disjoint iff the multisets are Multiset-disjoint (share no element).
candidates.lean_statement_sketch: theorem disjoint_toFinset {s t : Multiset α} : Disjoint s.toFinset t.toFinset ↔ Multiset.Disjoint s t
candidates.proof_family_hint: rw [Finset.disjoint_left]; simp [Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.disjoint_left]; likely IS the failing theorem itself

candidates.informal_description: A multiset's toFinset equals {a} iff a is in s and every member of s equals a.
candidates.lean_statement_sketch: theorem toFinset_eq_singleton_iff {s : Multiset α} {a : α} : s.toFinset = {a} ↔ a ∈ s ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, x = a
candidates.proof_family_hint: rw [Finset.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem]; simp [Multiset.mem_toFinset]; likely IS the failing theorem itself

candidates.informal_description: Membership in n • s holds iff n ≠ 0 and membership in s; the membership lemma behind toFinset_nsmul.
candidates.lean_statement_sketch: theorem mem_nsmul {s : Multiset α} {a : α} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : a ∈ n • s ↔ a ∈ s
candidates.proof_family_hint: ext x <;> simp [Multiset.mem_toFinset, Multiset.mem_nsmul]; toFinset_nsmul reduces to this membership bridge under n ≠ 0

candidates.informal_description: NOT a lemma: the genuinely-missing reusable capability is a tactic family `ext x <;> simp [Multiset.mem_toFinset, <side lemma>]` (and the Finset-characterization rewrites) for Multiset.toFinset goals — the failures are membership/extensionality goals mis-served by the Multiset induction oracle.
candidates.lean_statement_sketch: N/A (tactic family / probe, candidate SF3 action rather than a lemma)
candidates.proof_family_hint: ext / Finset.ext_iff + Multiset.mem_toFinset; the SF2 probe ladder tests whether this family closes all three
